belief.answer: An exact finite-rank formula is as follows. Set h=2g−2, N=4g−4, d=2g−1−k, Q=⌊N/k⌋, B=2h+1+dQ, and J=B+N+dQ+1. Put φ=φ_b(t), q=kt^kφ, and a=−½t^(−h)(1−t^(4g+2))^(1/2). On polynomials in w modulo w^(N+1), let P be the substitution matrix F(u)↦F(tw(1−qw^k)^(−1/k)), and let D and C be the multiplication matrices of 1−qw^k and −t^(−1)−t^kφ′w^k, respectively. Define T_O=P, T_L=aDP, and T_S=[[aP,0],[aCP,DP]]. Let H_B consist of the even integers from 0 to B and the odd integers from 2g+1 to B. Set F_s=t^(−s) for even s and F_s=t^(−s)(1−t^(4g+2))^(1/2) for odd s. For any m×m matrix T among T_O,T_L,T_S, define the finite complex matrix M(T), with rows (α,j), 1≤α≤m, 1≤j≤J, and columns (i,s), 1≤i≤m, s∈H_B, by M(T)_((α,j),(i,s))=[t^(−j)](a^(−1)(T^(−transpose))_(αi)F_s). Then \boxed{\Delta_b=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_S)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_O)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_L)}. All powers are expanded at t=0 with the specified square-root branch.
